answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can submit bids, and caps bids per bonded identity. An agent selling a pearl or buying a whisper of market data follows the same rule. Fake accounts cannot create free bidding capacity: each adds another locked bond. To spiral from ten identities to ten thousand, an attacker must immobilize a thousand times more capital, sacrificing liquidity and interest for the full lock period.
